concerns.asked: Likely: show that the emission is not surface electric-dipole radiation, photo-Dember or demagnetization.
concerns.response: A new paragraph (p. 3) argues surface emission is unlikely dominant because the pattern orientation is fixed with fluence and temperature, citing CrSiTe3 surface emission; p. 4 adds a demagnetization argument; p. 2 notes only the p-projection is detected.
concerns.judgment: The text now engages the alternatives directly, which is what a referee would likely ask first. Whether arguments without a control measurement were enough cannot be judged without the report.
concerns.still_open: No measurement (applied field, transmission, thickness, reference sample) separates the mechanisms.

concerns.asked: Likely: explain how the effect differs from inverse Faraday and Cotton-Mouton effects and cite related nonlinear spin-generation theory.
concerns.response: The introduction (pp. 1-2) now contrasts the mechanisms and adds Kirilyuk et al. and Feng et al. (PRL 2025); p. 2 places the spin-orbit effects in Te-dominated bands.
concerns.judgment: The comparison and citations are now in place.
concerns.still_open: No material-specific estimate of the susceptibility appears in the main text.

concerns.asked: Likely: give evidence that the 45-degree polarity reversal and minimum come from two competing magnetization components.
concerns.response: A new Fig. 3d panel compares the 0.4 mJ/cm2 waveform with the sum of the 0.1 and 0.75 mJ/cm2 waveforms (p. 4 caption, p. 6 text); p. 4 writes the far-field projection n_z M_y - n_y M_z.
concerns.judgment: A direct decomposition test was added, which goes to the heart of the likely request.
concerns.still_open: The test is at 0.4 mJ/cm2 while the text puts the minimum near 0.2 mJ/cm2, and it does not by itself show the components are magnetic.

concerns.asked: Likely: show directly that the ferromagnetic moment changes, or narrow the claim.
concerns.response: The discussion (p. 6) names time-resolved XMCD as future validation, and the introduction (p. 2) now says the authors 'argue' the density 'may act' as an internal field.
concerns.judgment: The limitation is acknowledged but the title and abstract still claim manipulation of ferromagnetism.
concerns.still_open: No direct magnetic probe of the pumped state.

concerns.asked: Likely: state how the error bars were obtained.
concerns.response: Fig. 2 (p. 3) and Fig. 4 (p. 5) captions define error bars from the spread over Fourier-transform windows.
concerns.still_open: The error bars reflect analysis choice only, not run-to-run or sample-to-sample variation.

concerns.asked: Possibly: say whether the full THz field vector was measured.
concerns.response: p. 2 now states that only the p-projection is detected.

concerns.asked: Possibly: clarify how a single-domain model applies to the illuminated spot.
concerns.response: p. 4 says the model takes the spatial average of the Cr moments over the beam spot.
concerns.judgment: This states the assumption but does not discuss domains or the field history; sufficiency depends on what was asked.
concerns.still_open: Net out-of-plane magnetization at zero field in a soft ferromagnet is not discussed.

concerns.response: Data are now in a Source Data file (p. 6).
concerns.judgment: Met, probably also by journal policy.

concerns.asked: Possibly: present the mechanism as an interpretation rather than a demonstration.
concerns.response: The introduction (p. 2) now says the authors 'attribute' the effect and 'argue' it 'may act' as an internal field.
concerns.judgment: The body is softer, but the abstract keeps 'demonstrate' and 'quantitatively captured'.

concerns.asked: Possibly: justify the claim that the mechanism is widely applicable.
concerns.response: The outlook (p. 6) now gives the symmetry condition: slow modes transforming like E x E.
concerns.judgment: A concrete condition replaces the bare claim.
